voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: Paris, May nineteen twenty-seven. Twelve days before Lindbergh, a white biplane took off to fly non-stop to New York.
Soon after take-off, it dropped its landing gear to save weight. It was meant to land on the water at New York.
It was seen leaving the French coast. A Paris newspaper reported it had arrived. It never did.
People in Newfoundland and Maine reported hearing an engine. None of it was ever confirmed.
Decades of searches have found no confirmed wreckage. The only piece known is the landing gear it dropped.
